cim: New course introduces students to AI at Western Nevada College
cim_eredeti: New course introduces students to AI at Western Nevada College
szoveg_eredeti:
Western Nevada College is offering Introduction to Artificial Intelligence, a hybrid computer information technology course during the spring semester.

Western Nevada College announces the debut of Introduction to Artificial Intelligence, a hybrid computer information technology course during the spring semester.

The 16-week course introduces students to the foundations of AI, with an emphasis on large language models, their capabilities and limitations. Students gain three skills from the course: how to use AI to automate tasks for themselves, how to build AI agents that automate tasks for others and how to use AI to design and build software of their own invention.

Students automate a task they repeat every week. They build an agent with the checks that make it safe for someone else to use. They write a specification for software they thought of, then build it and test it.

The course is platform-agnostic, so the skills carry over to whatever AI tools a workplace uses. No previous programming experience is required. Students learn Python and Git in the opening weeks. They need a computer where they can store software and a pro account with either Claude or ChatGPT.

WNC earns national honor for engaging students in voting, democracy

WNC has received the ALL IN Most Engaged Campus for College Student Voting award.

The recognition places WNC among 273 colleges and universities nationwide honored by the ALL IN Campus Democracy Challenge out of more than 1,000 participating institutions.

The recognition celebrates institutions that demonstrate a commitment to institutionalizing nonpartisan democratic engagement and increasing college student voter participation.

To qualify, institutions were required to meet three criteria:

• Submit a nonpartisan democratic engagement action plan to ALL IN

• Earn the 2026 Highly Established Action Plan Seal for developing a strong action plan

• Have a current signatory to the ALL IN Presidents' Commitment to Full Student Voter Participation

Registration is underway for spring semester.

The spring semester begins Monday, Jan. 25. Students interested in getting an earlier start can also explore winter session offerings, with five-week courses beginning Monday, Dec. 21, and three-week courses starting Monday, Jan. 4.

For registration assistance, call 775-445-3277 or email [email protected]. To schedule an academic advising appointment, visit wncadvising.youcanbook.me. Students on the Fallon campus, call 775-445-3379.
